newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks gain one pct, rise for fourth day.
newsitem.headline: India stocks gain one pct, rise for fourth day.

text.p: Indian shares rose on Thursday for the fourth consecutive session this week, helped by fund buying and political developments, dealers said.
Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao on Thursday stepped down as chief of the Congress party's parliamentary delegation amid a flurry of corruption charges, his aides said.
"He has resigned. He has sent a letter to the Congress president and secretary just before 4 p.m. (1030 GMT)," Chetan Sharma, one of Rao's assistants, told Reuters by telephone.
"I submit my resignation from the leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP)," Sharma quoted Rao's single-line letter as saying.
Marketmen said prices rallied just before close of trade on expectations that former finance minister Manmohan Singh might take over from Rao.
"This (Rao's resignation) might be reflected in tomorrow's prices...in anticipation of favourable developments," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at broker Pashupati Advani.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's shaky ruling United Front coalition depends on Congress for make-or-break support.
Scattered buying by the Unit Trust of India, the country's biggest mutual fund, in blue-chip shares such as Hind Lever and Bajaj Auto pepped market sentiment, dealers said.
"Today's session was mainly of a speculative nature as both buyers and sellers equally dominated trading...," said Manoj Choraria of Delhi brokers Choraria Investments.

SBI gained 3.0 rupees to 221.50, Reliance 3.25 to 197.55, Hind Lever 10.20 to 806.75, ACC 22.50 to 1,152.0, TISCO 2.0 to 161.0, Bajaj Auto 18.70 to 816.0 and M&M 3.50 to 331.75. The National Stock Exchange index rose 0.18 points to 860.58.
